denied.label: Denied, then appealed
denied.blurb: Lumbar fusion for Rosalind Petrakis against Cascade — a legacy payer with no FHIR surface at all. Two criteria are genuinely short at submission.

run.m: Case PA-2026-0460 opened manually by a coordinator from the surgical scheduling worklist.
run.d: No CDS Hook — Cascade Valley Spine Institute runs an EHR whose hook support is not enabled at this site. The order arrived as an HL7 v2 ORM.

run.m: No CRD service published by Cascade Mutual. Falling back to the cached policy store.
run.d: This is the tier CMS-0057-F exists to remove, and the tier you still have to support in the meantime. Authorisation requirement determined from a policy document, not an API.

run.m: Coverage confirmed by X12 270/271 only. No benefit detail, no document list, no cost share.
Querying 4 connected sources across the health system.
Retrieved: spine surgery evaluation 2026-09-18, PT course summary 2026-08-11, MRI lumbar 2026-07-02, structured social history.
No behavioural health screening instrument found in 12 months. PHQ-9, GAD-7 and equivalents all returned zero.
Loading Cascade CM-ORT-22633 rev 2025-11 — 4 criteria, all required.
C1 six months of conservative care — PARTIAL (0.55).
run.d: The note claims care since April 2026, about 5 months. Contemporaneous documentation only covers 2026-05-04 to 2026-08-11 — 14 weeks. The gap between what is asserted and what is documented is exactly what a reviewer will find.

run.m: C2 imaging demonstrating instability — PARTIAL (0.61).
run.d: The MRI shows grade I anterolisthesis, which the policy accepts. But it is a static supine study and the report itself says dynamic instability cannot be assessed. Flexion-extension films are the study this criterion is written for.

run.m: C3 behavioural health screening — GAP. Nothing on file.
C4 tobacco cessation — NOT MET (0.20). Social history records a current every-day smoker with no cessation programme documented.
Packet confidence 0.41. The agent recommends not submitting.
run.d: Two criteria are short and two have no evidence at all. The honest recommendation is to hold, obtain a PHQ-9 and flexion-extension films, and check the cessation record before filing.

run.m: Routing to human review with a recommendation against submission.
run.d: The surgery is booked for three weeks' time, so a coordinator may submit anyway to preserve the timeline and appeal if needed. The demo takes that path deliberately.

review.confLabel: Low — two partial criteria and two with no evidence

criteria.rationale: The surgeon's note asserts conservative care since April 2026. The contemporaneous record supports 2026-05-04 to 2026-08-11, which is 14 weeks, not 6 months. An assertion in a note is not the same as documentation, and reviewers treat it that way.

Grade I anterolisthesis is documented and correlates with the symptomatic level. But the report explicitly states that dynamic instability cannot be assessed on a static supine study, and this criterion is written for flexion-extension films.
No PHQ-9, GAD-7 or equivalent instrument exists in any connected source within 12 months. The screening is inexpensive and can be done in clinic; it simply has not been.

Structured social history records a current every-day smoker as of 2026-09-18, with no cessation documentation attached. On the evidence available at submission, this criterion is affirmatively not met.

qs.a: MRI 2026-07-02 — grade I anterolisthesis, static study

gaps: C3 — no behavioural health screening on file. A PHQ-9 takes two minutes in clinic.
C4 — the record shows a current smoker with no cessation documentation. If the patient has in fact stopped, the record does not say so.
C2 — flexion-extension radiographs have not been performed. This is the study the criterion is written for.
Submitting in this state is a deliberate trade-off to preserve the surgical date, not a recommendation.

outcome.note: Illustrative. Denial letters in practice are often vaguer than this and arrive as scanned PDFs, which is why OCR sits in the integration layer.

denied.letter:
Cascade Mutual Assurance
Utilisation Management — Appeals Unit
Re: Appeal of adverse determination CMA-UM-441902
Member: Rosalind Petrakis · CMA-3390-70112 · DOB 1959-01-27
Procedure: CPT 22633 / 22853, L4-L5 transforaminal interbody fusion
Policy cited: CM-ORT-22633 rev 2025-11, criteria C1 and C2

To the reviewing physician,

This appeal responds to the determination dated 2026-09-29, which cited two criteria. Evidence answering one of them was completed after the original submission; evidence answering the other existed at the time but was held in a system outside the submitting practice. Both are attached.

C2 — imaging demonstrating segmental instability.
Flexion-extension radiographs of the lumbar spine were performed on 2026-09-25 and demonstrate 6 mm of anterior translation of L4 on L5 between flexion and extension, at the symptomatic level. This is the dynamic study the criterion contemplates, and it meets the radiographic threshold for segmental instability. The original submission included only the 2026-07-02 MRI, a static supine study whose own report states that dynamic instability cannot be assessed. That limitation is now addressed.
[Exhibit A — DiagnosticReport/dxr-9014, Cascade Valley Imaging, 2026-09-25]

C1 — six months of structured conservative care.
We do not contend that six months of care is documented. The contemporaneous record supports fourteen weeks of supervised physical therapy between 2026-05-04 and 2026-08-11, together with continuous gabapentin and activity modification from April 2026. We ask the reviewer to consider §2.1(b) of the policy, which permits the duration requirement to be shortened where there is documented progressive neurological compromise. Ambulation tolerance fell from 110 m to under 100 m between August and September 2026 despite ongoing therapy, and the plateau is documented in the therapist's own discharge note.
[Exhibit B — Composition/b2c9d771, Cascade Valley Rehab, 2026-08-11]

Additional criteria, addressed pre-emptively.
Behavioural health screening (C3) was completed on 2026-09-26: PHQ-9 total score 4, indicating minimal symptoms and no untreated condition expected to affect surgical outcome. Tobacco cessation (C4) commenced 2026-08-14 through a structured programme with nicotine replacement; a carbon monoxide breath test on 2026-09-22 returned 4 ppm, consistent with sustained abstinence of approximately six weeks at the time of this appeal.
[Exhibit C — Observation/obs-44877 and Composition/cc4419]

We respectfully request reconsideration on the basis of the dynamic imaging now available, and are available for peer-to-peer review at the reviewer's convenience.

Prepared from the patient record by the Denial & Appeal Agent and reviewed, edited and submitted under the signature of:

Noor Abbasi, MD — Cascade Valley Spine Institute
NPI 1234567890 (fabricated) · 2026-09-29

appealSubmit.m: Letter reviewed and edited by Dr. Abbasi. Two sentences on the C1 exception clause rewritten; exhibits unchanged. Signed and released.
appealSubmit.d: The edit is recorded as a diff against the agent's draft. Over time, that diff is the training signal worth more than the draft itself.

appealSubmit.m: Filing through the Cascade appeals portal with three exhibits. Peer-to-peer requested.
Appeal received, reference CMA-APL-30188. Peer-to-peer scheduled 2026-10-02, 14:20.
Briefing sheet delivered to Dr. Abbasi's in-basket ahead of the call: one page, the cited criterion, the answering exhibit, and the C1 concession stated plainly.
Patient informed that an appeal has been filed, what it argues, and when the review call is scheduled.

appealOutcome.title: Appeal filed — awaiting peer-to-peer
meta: Exhibits: 3 (dynamic imaging, PT course, screening + cessation)
Human touches: 1 coordinator approval, 1 physician signature
appealOutcome.body: The prototype stops here deliberately. An appeal outcome depends on a conversation between two physicians, and no honest demo should simulate that. What the system can claim is narrower and more defensible: the deadline was tracked, the answering evidence was found — including a record the practice did not know existed — and the physician spent minutes on a letter rather than an afternoon.
appealOutcome.note: Illustrative. Overturn rates on first-level appeals vary enormously by payer, service line and how specific the original denial was.
